survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses PIRLS 2021 Ireland data collected from a two-stage sample of schools and intact/reconstituted class groups, with exclusions for ineligible pupils (e.g., leaving school, teacher-exemptions) and non-participation on test day. The analytic results are presented as weighted estimates (e.g., weighted response rates and weighted percentages), indicating that sampling/participation weights were applied to make estimates representative of the target population of pupils in the relevant grade level in Ireland. The manuscript does not name a specific weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT) and does not report replicate-weight methodology (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so replicate-weight usage cannot be confirmed. Because this is a descriptive large-scale assessment report (not an ML modeling paper), the weighting is used for population-representative estimation rather than for predictive model training.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Target population was pupils completing Fourth Class in 2021; for Ireland (Start G5), the sampled Grade 4 pupils were assessed in autumn 2021 after progressing to Fifth Class. Sampling used a two-stage design: (1) a representative sample of 151 schools stratified by DEIS status, language of instruction, and gender intake; 148 schools had eligible pupils and all participated. (2) Within each school, up to two Fourth Class groups were selected (all pupils if ≤2 groups; otherwise two groups randomly selected). Exclusions between sampling and testing included pupils who left their schools (130) and a small number exempted by teachers due to disabilities and/or limited English proficiency (53). On test day, 303 pupils were absent and 11 were withdrawn by parents, leaving 4,663 pupils who participated in the PIRLS test. Questionnaire response rates were high among test participants (e.g., 99.6% Pupil Questionnaire; 93.2% Home Questionnaire; 97.2% Teacher Questionnaire; 99.2% School Questionnaire).

data.outcome_summary: This PIRLS 2021 national report provides descriptive achievement results for Ireland’s Start G5 cohort (autumn 2021), with 4,663 pupils participating in the PIRLS test. Pupils’ mean reading achievement was 577 (SE 2.5), significantly above the PIRLS scale centrepoint (500) and higher than most other Start G5 countries, though comparisons are cautioned due to the Start G5 vs End G4 design and COVID-19 disruption. Achievement shows strong equity gradients: girls scored 11 points higher than boys (583 vs 573), and SES is strongly associated with achievement (highest vs lowest SES quartile: 620 vs 536; High benchmark 88% vs 45%; Advanced 48% vs 10%). The report also finds relative strengths on Literary texts and Interpret/Evaluate processes, and relative weaknesses on Informational texts and Retrieve/Infer processes. Contextual questionnaire analyses indicate that reading behaviours and attitudes are positively associated with achievement, while wellbeing indicators (tiredness/hunger) and bullying are negatively associated; however, the report cautions against causal interpretation.
